VERIFIED twice over. (1) Published key: Skowron & Friedlander (1998) Appendix gives ER = items 1,6,10,14,18,21,26,30,34,38,40 and EC = 2,3,8,12,16,20,24,28,32,36,39,42. Our 16 item texts split by content into professional devaluation/microinvalidations (mi1-mi8: 'people expect less of me because I am a woman', 'suggestions are more likely to be accepted if made by a man') and sexualization/objectification (mi9-mi16: inappropriate compliments, suggestive jokes, comments on dress). Tested against the live correlation structure: 15/16 items load strongest on their own factor, the sole exception being mi16 (0.32 own vs 0.36 rival) -- marginal. This matches the paper's own two-factor solution. Subscale membership verified; order within a factor not separated.

Each Kirby MCQ item text states its own immediate/delayed amounts and delay, so it implies a discount rate k=(LDR-SIR)/(SIR*delay). Parsed k from our item_text for all 27 items and correlated it with the live proportion choosing the delayed option (resp=2): Spearman rho=+0.961, Pearson on log k =+0.961, in the correct direction, with the extremes exactly as theory requires (k=0.00016 items: 4-7% choose delayed; k=0.25 items: 97%). Items sharing a k differ only by reward magnitude, the expected magnitude effect. A permuted item_text mapping would destroy this relationship, so this is a strong item-by-item verification. Also confirms the codes follow canonical Kirby ordering (mc1 = $54 vs $55/117d).

'Q15: ...'), and the supplementary data file's columns are literally Q1..Q15. The tie is an explicit label match, not an order inference, so no statistical check is needed. Our 15 item texts match Table 1 verbatim and fall in its three stated blocks (Motivation Q1-Q5, Participation Q6-Q10, Effectiveness Q11-Q15). NOTE: the separate table-name misattribution issue stands -- the table is named 'alomari' but the paper is Xie et al., DOI 10.1371/journal.pone.0340806 (PMC12810817).

Found labels the extraction had missed: the PLOS supplementary .sav files label every GCBS item (s003 GCBS1..15, s004 GCBS01..15). In the live data SEV24_5 is the only item with 8 levels and the other four are 1-5, so item 5 is pinned and the numbering scheme is confirmed consistent. No per-item statistics published, but the resp is days-per-week consumption, which is highly diagnostic of food group. Live means line up coherently with the assigned labels: maize 5.01 (staple, 38% at 7 days) > tubers 4.24 / fish 4.33 > rice 3.54 > vegetables 2.95 > eggs 1.57 > milk/dairy 1.20, meat 1.84/1.97. A permuted mapping would put dairy or eggs at staple frequency. Rules out a random permutation; does not prove adjacent pairs (e.g. meat-livestock vs meat-poultry, 1.84 vs 1.97) are not swapped.

The CSES has 6 positively-worded and 6 reverse-worded items, canonically at odd and even positions respectively. Our item_text follows that exactly (CSE1/3/5/7/9/11 positive, CSE2/4/6/8/10/12 negative), and the live data are RAW (not reverse-scored), so the keying shows up directly in the correlation matrix: CSE1 correlates +0.31..+0.45 with every odd item and -0.06..-0.36 with every even item. The odd/even block split is clean across all 12 items, so each item's polarity class is verified -- a permutation moving a negative item into an odd slot would flip the sign pattern. Does not separate items within a polarity class. (Note: the near-zero corrected item-total correlations are an artifact of summing a raw mixed-keying scale, not a problem.)

Content match is exact: all 9 items are the canonical German UWES-9 wording in canonical order (UWES1 'voll ueberschaeumender Energie' = VI1, UWES5 'Wenn ich morgens aufstehe' = VI3, UWES8 'gehe voellig in meiner Arbeit auf' = AB2, etc.). Correlation-block test on the canonical assignment (vigor 1,2,5 / dedication 3,4,7 / absorption 6,8,9): 6/9 items load strongest on their own subscale. The vigor triad and the dedication triad are all correct; the three absorption items (6,8,9) load marginally higher on dedication (e.g. UWES9 own=0.63 vs DE=0.67). That is a known property of the UWES-9 -- dedication and absorption are nearly collinear -- not evidence of a bad mapping, so the test cannot separate those two facets here. Chain, for the record: IRW item = the study CSV's own column name (UWES1..UWES9, melted unrenamed), so the join key is inference-free; item text = official German UWES-9 PDF (wilmarschaufeli.nl/publications/Schaufeli/Tests/UWES_D_9.pdf), which numbers items 1-9; the text-to-code tie is number-to-number. No codebook exists in the figshare record to upgrade this to data_labels.

Weak route only. The SWLS is unidimensional with all items on one 1-7 scale, so no block or range structure exists, and the live per-item means are tightly clustered (3.69-3.97) -- too close to identify items even if the paper published them. One canonical marker holds: item 5 ('If I could live my life over, I would change almost nothing'), reliably the lowest-endorsed SWLS item, is indeed the lowest here at 3.69. That pins item 5 only. WHOQOL-BREF domain-block test (physical 3,4,10,15-18 / psychological 5,6,7,11,19,26 / social 20,21,22 / environment 8,9,12-14,23-25): 18/24 domain items load strongest on their own domain. Middling, and expected to be -- the BREF's four domains are strongly intercorrelated and items 3, 4 and 26 are reverse-worded but NOT reverse-scored in the live data, which distorts the physical and psychological blocks. Supporting evidence for those three: whoqol_4 is the only item with a negative corrected item-total (-0.11) and whoqol_3 (0.04) and whoqol_26 (0.08) are among the lowest -- exactly the canonical reverse-keyed triple, which pins those 3 items.
